name: Minn. Stat. 115.061 Duty to notify; avoiding water pollution (public notice paragraph (c), 2023 c 60; amended 2026 c 79)
access_detail: Current text fetched (raw/mn-stat-115-061.html); 2024 version (raw/mn-stat-115-061-2024.html) and 2026 c 79 (H.F. 4224, raw/mn-2026-c79-section1.txt) compared: 2026 added "of the discharge", "downstream users, including the" public and "Tribal governments".
status_reason: Public notice duty for every POTW and domestic sewer owner after any discharge; channel may be in person, phone, radio, social media or web page; signs at impacted public use areas. No hour deadline ("Promptly").
notes: (a): "it is the duty of every person to notify the agency immediately of the discharge, accidental or otherwise, of any substance or material under its control which, if not recovered, may cause pollution of waters of the state". (c) Promptly after notifying the agency of a discharge under paragraph (a), a publicly owned treatment works or a publicly or privately owned domestic sewer system owner must provide notice of the discharge to potentially impacted downstream users, including the public, Tribal governments, and drinking water facilities. Notice must be made using the most efficient communications system available to the facility owner such as in person, telephone call, radio, social media, web page, or another expedited form. In addition, signage must be posted at all impacted public use areas within the same jurisdiction or notification must be provided to the entity that has jurisdiction over any impacted public use areas. A notice under this paragraph must include the date and time of the discharge, a description of the material released, a warning of the potential public health risk, and the permittee's contact information.

name: MPCA "Public Notification of Wastewater Releases: Notice to Downstream Users and Drinking Water Intakes" (wq-wwprm1-43, October 2026)
status_reason: Defines whom to notify: "Any location within 25 miles downstream of the release which the public could encounter the receiving water"; "Notification should also be given when the release has ended."
notes: Steps: "1. Immediately report the incident to the Minnesota Duty Officer (800-422-0798). 2. Promptly after notifying the Duty Officer, provide notice to the potentially impacted downstream users, including the public, and Tribal governments, and any drinking water facilities." Notice "shall communicate the recent wastewater release data and the risks of contact with the water and/or soil, including but not limited to date, time, quantity, quality (if available at the time of notification), material in the discharge, a warning of public health risk, and the permittee or responsible party's contact information."

name: Minnesota Duty Officer Program (DPS/BCA): one-call reporting of all discharges
operator: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Criminal Apprehension
access_detail: Phone 800-422-0798, 24/7. No public incident list found. MPCA says its emergency response staff field more than 3,000 incident reports a year.
status_reason: Every wastewater release is reported here first, but the reports are not published; a 2017 compilation for a legislative commission ("MPCA - 2017 Municipal Wastewater Release Data") shows the data exist.
